Young Men's Christian Association of Montreal 


For release after 2:00 p.m, 
Thursday, April 17, 1969, 
Approximately 180 words, 


COSTS OF INACTIVITY HIGH 
BUT EFFECTS REVERSIBLE 


A national expert on physical fitness Thursday warned a 
Montreal Lions Club luncheon that many thousands of Canadians are 


heedlessly squandering years of life and well being, 


“Physical activity is one of the main causes of premature 
deterioration, Yet some of the world's best brains continue seeking 
new ways to reduce manual effort," said Alex Wright, Physical Education 


Director of the Montreal Downtown YMCA, 


“That's progress. We don't want to fight it. Our objective 
at the Y is to offer urgently needed substitutes for the type of 


natural movement so essential to fitness." 


He emphasized that pills may mask or ease the symptoms, but 
only planned exercise can prevent unfitness and reverse the effects 
of its accompanying decline in resistance to cardiovascular disease, 


endurance and general capacity for living, 


‘Sweevel weaes

Fortunately, he said, even the effects of years of indolence 
can generally be offset--and in a relatively short time--by planned 


exercise, 


"Our on-going tests indicate adult males in sedentary occu- 
pations can, in just three months, improve the efficiency of their 
heart and circulatory systems by some 35%, and drop about 10 lbs. 


of excess fat while doing so," 


"The gain after a year of involvement in our program is 
about 70-75% for cardiovascular fitness, Body weight is also, 
usually, what it should be,
